title: A non-power-of-two row width closes every lowering route for RMSNorm on sm_103a: the whole row is refused by Triton's arange rule, the tiled two-pass is refused by its loop-nest rule, and native_cuda declares no reduce at all

evidence.note: No campaign and no device. Compiler.assess probes at this commit, plus a model-driven rewrite of 75 harvested candidates across 15 FlashInfer-Bench tasks whose ledgers live outside the checkout at open-cake-ir-experiments/fib-extraction/ledgers/. Only the probes below are load-bearing; the rewrite is what pointed at this task.

All five candidates for hidden size 7168 end in a backend refusal, while 001 (h2048) and 002 (h4096) produce eight accepted and lowering-eligible Schedules between them. The operator, the ABI and the authoring path are identical across the three tasks; the row width is the only difference, and 7168 is the only one of the three that is not a power of two.

Two rules close the two ways to write it, and they are not the same kind of rule. Lines 271-280 refuse a whole-row tile: TRITON_ARANGE_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED, 'a positive power-of-two span'. That one is faithful -- tl.arange genuinely requires it. Lines 476-486 refuse the tiled two-pass: when tile_loops > 1 the route requires exactly two loops at depths [0, 1], a nest. RMSNorm's two passes are siblings at depth [0, 0] -- accumulate the sum of squares over tiles, then re-read and normalize -- and the second cannot nest inside the first because normalization needs the completed sum. Triton itself writes two sequential for loops without difficulty; this bound is the emitter's shape, not the language's.

Line 23: SUPPORTED_OPERATION_KINDS is {cast, elementwise, load, mma, reduce_argmin, store}. It carries reduce_argmin and not reduce, so the route that has no arange rule and no loop-nest rule cannot express the reduction this operator is. Measured through the boundary: BACKEND_OPERATION_UNEMITTABLE, "backend 'native_cuda' has no body for operation kind 'reduce'". triton, metal and cutedsl all declare reduce; native_cuda is the exception.

Both spellings written by hand and put through Compiler.assess at this commit, so the corner is walked rather than inferred. The tiled form reaches accepted=True with lowering_eligible=False and exactly one finding, TRITON_LOOP_NEST_UNSUPPORTED -- the Schedule is well-formed and the IR admits an arbitrary number of tile_loops; only the emitter refuses. Two diagnostics cost a repair round each on the way and are worth their own note: lm.range rejects an 'axis' keyword without saying it wants dimension and tile, and lm.reduce(across_loop=True) is refused as 'the historical omitted spelling' without saying that omitting it is the fix. Both name the violated contract; neither names the satisfying form.

At source 5a0c916b, canonical Compiler.lower for the 7168-wide two-pass sm_103a fixture compiled offline under Triton 3.7.1 and produced CUBIN, PTX, TTIR, TTGIR and LLIR. This is compilation, not device execution.

Broker-managed shared correctness check of the fixed emitted two-pass slice: structured and random inputs at [32,512,7168] had zero mismatches to an independent PyTorch row-sum-times-input reference, finite outputs and unchanged inputs. It did not run the original RMSNorm workload or measure performance; no Executor Revision was instantiated.

observation: This is a lowering gap, not a vocabulary gap, and the distinction decides who owns it. The IR says the program fine: tile_loops is a list, a sibling pair parses, and the Schedule is accepted. What refuses is a backend's implemented shape in one case and a backend's declared capability set in the other. It also shows why a single task cannot find this. Read alone, 003's five refusals look like five candidates that failed; read beside 001 and 002 -- same operator, same ABI, eight accepted Schedules -- the row width is the only variable, and a shape-triggered route limit becomes visible. The corpus's value here was to put three widths of one operator side by side, not to supply a kernel worth copying.
proposed_change: Two separable changes, and the arange rule is not among them -- it is correct and must stay. (a) Widen the Triton emitter to admit sibling tile loops at the same depth, which is a slice shape it does not currently generate rather than a Triton limitation; the guard at backends/triton.py:476-486 encodes 'one outer with one inner' as the only multi-loop form. (b) Or declare and implement reduce in native_cuda's SUPPORTED_OPERATION_KINDS, which removes the arange constraint from the path entirely. Either one alone unblocks the operator; (a) is the narrower change and (b) closes a capability asymmetry that reduce_argmin's presence makes odd. Both are P7 changes: the emitter or the capability set moves together with the analyses that read it, and the Corpus Gate runs on the commit. Separately and smaller: give the two diagnostics above their satisfying form, since a refusal that does not say what would be accepted costs the author a round each time.
